calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Bruins are one of the league’s best for chance quality, but the Golden Knights are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Hot take: the Golden Knights shut it down.
calls.call: The Golden Knights keep the Bruins’ chances less dangerous than the league average (a 6.4% chance of scoring on the average shot).
calls.nums: Boston 4th for chance quality (a 6.7% chance of scoring on the average shot) · Vegas 4th for preventing dangerous shots

calls.happened: On chance quality, Boston had 4.3% a shot tonight, against a league average of 6.4% a shot. They usually sit at 6.7% a shot.

calls.head: A shadow job for Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens
calls.body: At home, the Bruins keep sending Lindholm’s line (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Marco Sturm has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Golden Knights’ first line is Barbashev, Eichel and Stone.
calls.call: The Bruins’ L2 (Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens) spends at least 54% of its 5-on-5 time against the Golden Knights’ first line, against about 38% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 71% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 38% with no line matching
calls.cite: Matchups · Boston home games this season · 7 games, 48 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 38% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Boston’s L2 (Mittelstadt, Lindholm, Hagens) spent 79% of its 5-on-5 time against Vegas’s L1 (9:49 of 12:27). The call needed 54%, halfway from the 38% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 71%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Sturm got his matchup
calls.plain: Boston sent Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the Golden Knights’ first line for 79% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 38% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Marco Sturm would send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the Golden Knights’ first line again

calls.head: There’s no curse: Swayman vs. The Golden Knights
calls.body: Swayman has been shaky against the Golden Knights since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Swayman starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .875 against the Golden Knights.

calls.happened: Jeremy Swayman stopped 21 of 23 shots (.913), against his usual .906 and his .875 against this team before tonight.

calls.title: The usual Swayman
calls.plain: Swayman played like his usual self, not like his record against the Golden Knights. Just a coincidence, as we said.
calls.said: Swayman’s rough record against the Golden Knights was a coincidence, and he’d look like himself

calls.head: The Golden Knights’ defense joins the attack, the Bruins’ stays home
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Vegas is one of the league’s best, but Boston is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Golden Knights’ defensemen jump into the play.

surprises.head: Boston couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Boston’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.3% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.7% (about 6.3% against Vegas) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Pastrňák seals it in the shootout
paras: James Hagens opened the scoring for the Bruins early in the first, and Morgan Geekie pushed the lead to 2-0 on the power play early in the second. Mark Stone got the Golden Knights on the board on the power play midway through the period. Trevor Connelly tied it 2-2 early in the third. David Pastrňák scored the only goal of the shootout for the Bruins.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. The Golden Knights hit two posts and still lost. Jeremy Swayman made 21 saves for the Bruins, and Carter Hart stopped 25 of 27 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Mitch Marner had the best night of anyone, even in a loss.

Braeden Bowman was thrown out with a five-minute major for elbowing and a game misconduct early in the second. Charlie McAvoy took three penalties on his own. The Bruins improved to 11-4-1, still first in the Atlantic, while the Golden Knights fell to 9-5-2, second in the Pacific.

items.text: Mitch Marner has a point in ten straight games.
Mitch Marner extended his point streak against Boston to eight games.
David Pastrňák extended his point streak against Vegas to six games.
Parker Wotherspoon faces his old team, Pittsburgh, on Tuesday.
